question: Should Discord Activity support be rebuilt under the Canvas/Discord plugin contracts with fail-closed Activity auth, continued through the newer overlapping branch after repair, or paused?
rationale: The unresolved choice crosses plugin ownership, Gateway authorization, token transport, operator config shape, and overlapping branches, so automation can identify defects but should not choose the permanent Activity security boundary.

options.title: Rebuild under plugin auth
options.body: Port the work to `extensions/canvas` and `extensions/discord`, require explicit Activity credentials, avoid URL tokens, bound fanout, and add live Discord proof before merge.

options.title: Continue through the newer branch
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/65205 as the working branch only after its security, compatibility, proof, and merge-state blockers are resolved.

options.title: Pause the feature
options.body: Leave Discord Activities out until maintainers settle whether the security model belongs in the Canvas plugin, Discord plugin, or an external package.

recommendation.title: Rebuild under plugin auth
recommendation.body: Port the work to `extensions/canvas` and `extensions/discord`, require explicit Activity credentials, avoid URL tokens, bound fanout, and add live Discord proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The blocking choice is primarily a product/security boundary decision around Canvas exposure and Gateway auth.
